landing.dns.page_title: DNS antiphishing — un toque, sin aplicación
landing.dns.page_description: Instala el resolutor DNS antiphishing de Cleanway en 30 segundos en iPhone, Android, Mac o Windows. Protección en todo el sistema, sin VPN ni aplicación.
landing.dns.hero_title: Bloquea el phishing en cada aplicación — sin instalar ninguna
landing.dns.hero_subtitle: Cleanway opera un resolutor DNS que filtra el phishing. Apunta tu teléfono o portátil hacia él y cada aplicación del dispositivo —Safari, Chrome, Mail, apps bancarias— recibe la misma protección.
landing.dns.hero_meta: Funciona en iOS 14+, iPadOS 14+, macOS 11+, Android 9+, Windows 11. Sin VPN. Sin gasto de batería.
landing.dns.ios_intro: Pulsa el botón inferior desde tu iPhone o iPad. iOS te pedirá permiso para instalar un perfil de configuración.
landing.dns.ios_step1: Pulsa «Permitir» cuando iOS solicite descargar el perfil.
landing.dns.ios_step2: Abre Ajustes → General → VPN y gestión de dispositivos → Cleanway DNS.
landing.dns.ios_step3: Pulsa «Instalar» dos veces e introduce el código de tu dispositivo.
landing.dns.ios_unsigned_note: Si iOS muestra «Sin firmar», es lo esperado: el programa de firma de Apple es de pago y preferimos no trasladarte ese coste. El perfil en sí es idéntico esté firmado o no.
landing.dns.android_intro: Android 9 (Pie) y posteriores incluyen DNS-over-TLS de fábrica — no hace falta ninguna app.
landing.dns.android_step1: Abre Ajustes → Redes e internet → DNS privado.
landing.dns.android_step2: Pulsa «Nombre de host del proveedor de DNS privado».
landing.dns.android_compat_note: Algunos Samsung y Xiaomi esconden la opción dentro de Conexiones → Más ajustes de conexión. Si no la encuentras, busca «DNS privado» en Ajustes.
landing.dns.win_intro: Windows 11 admite DNS-over-HTTPS de forma nativa. Las versiones anteriores de Windows requieren una herramienta de terceros, como Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 — lo sentimos.
landing.dns.win_step1: Abre Configuración → Redes e Internet → Wi-Fi → haz clic en tu red → Asignación de servidor DNS → Editar.
landing.dns.win_step2: Cambia a Manual, activa IPv4, define el DNS preferido en 1.1.1.1 y pon DNS sobre HTTPS en «Activado (plantilla manual)».
landing.dns.benefit_1: Los enlaces de phishing en SMS, correo y Telegram se abren como «sitio no encontrado» en lugar de una página que roba credenciales.
landing.dns.benefit_2: Los servidores de control de malware no pueden alcanzar tu dispositivo, ni siquiera si una app dudosa que instalaste intenta llamar a casa.
landing.dns.benefit_3: Los dominios que se hacen pasar por marcas (paypal-secure-login.com) se bloquean en el propio resolutor — tu navegador ni siquiera llega a cargarlos.
landing.dns.benefit_4: Funciona en cualquier app, no solo en el navegador. Enlaces de WhatsApp, apps bancarias, navegadores integrados — todo protegido.
landing.dns.privacy_heading: Privacidad — lo que vemos y lo que no
landing.dns.privacy_body: Cleanway DNS solo resuelve el dominio. No registramos las consultas en disco, no las enviamos a Sentry, no las vendemos a nadie. Las consultas viven en memoria justo el tiempo necesario para responder.
landing.dns.privacy_logs: Lo que SÍ guardamos: un contador diario anónimo del total de consultas y bloqueos, usado para publicar nuestro informe trimestral de transparencia. Sin dominios, sin IP, sin usuarios.
landing.dns.layer_heading: Where DNS fits in your protection
landing.dns.layer_body: DNS is the widest layer — it protects every app on your device, not just the browser. It is also the shallowest: it can only block a domain that is already on our phishing blocklist. It cannot read a page, so on its own it will not catch a brand-new phishing kit the moment it appears, or a credential form hiding on a trusted-but-hacked site.
landing.dns.layer_extension: For that deeper protection, add the Cleanway browser extension. It runs the full per-page analysis on every site you open, spots look-alike login forms in real time, and warns you before you type a password. DNS covers the widest surface; the extension adds the deepest checks — together they cover both.
landing.dns.layer_generic: This is not a generic DNS filter. Cleanway DNS is tuned specifically for phishing and credential theft, driven by the same threat intelligence that powers the extension — not a repurposed ad-blocking list.
landing.methodology.page_description: Cleanway's per-domain detection results vs Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 for Families, Google Safe Browsing, PhishTank, and VirusTotal — measured weekly on fresh URLhaus + PhishTank URLs. Reproducible benchmark script linked.
landing.methodology.hero_title: How we measure our own detection rate
landing.methodology.hero_subtitle: Every recall number we publish points here. The dataset, the script, and a button to clone it on GitHub.
landing.methodology.why_p1: Every other anti-phishing vendor publishes glossy quarterly threat reports without their false-positive rate or per-vendor recall comparison. The numbers exist only in their internal dashboards.
landing.methodology.why_p2: We do the opposite: this page runs the same Python script anyone can clone, every Monday, against fresh URLhaus + PhishTank phishing URLs, and publishes the raw results. The script's output IS the marketing claim.
landing.methodology.results_unavailable: Latest benchmark snapshot not available — re-running cron now.
landing.methodology.results_meta: Snapshot: $DATE$. Sample: $PHISHING$ phishing URLs, $LEGIT$ Tranco legit URLs.
landing.methodology.safe_table_heading: Legit batch (FPR — false-positive rate, expected verdict: safe)
landing.methodology.verdict_mapping_head: How we map each resolver's response
landing.methodology.verdict_mapping_p1: Different vendors return different verdict shapes. We normalise to three: dangerous / safe / unknown. Unknown verdicts (rate-limited, not indexed, error) are reported separately — not counted as right or wrong.
landing.methodology.reproduce_p1: Two commands and a Python 3 install. The script fetches the same feeds, runs the same comparisons, writes the same JSON output:
landing.methodology.cadence_p1: The benchmark runs every Monday at 05:15 UTC via a GitHub Actions cron. Results commit to docs/benchmarks/ in this repo. A regression-detection step opens a PR if recall drops more than 5 percentage points week-over-week.
landing.methodology.caveat_1: Cleanway uses the public /api/v1/check endpoint — same anonymous surface a regular user would see. We deliberately do NOT use a privileged path for benchmarking ourselves.
landing.methodology.caveat_2: PhishTank's free check API returns 'not indexed' for most fresh URLhaus URLs because their database lags by a few hours — that's why PhishTank's Recall column often shows '—' (unknown), not because it's broken.
landing.methodology.caveat_3: Google Safe Browsing requires an API key (GOOGLE_SAFE_BROWSING_KEY). If unset, that column shows '—' and is excluded from the comparison.
landing.methodology.caveat_4: Latency p50 measured from this script's host (US/EU CI runner); your latency from Asia or LATAM will differ. The relative comparison stays the same.

mobile.report.empty_body: Check a link and it will show up here.
mobile.report.share_message: My Cleanway week: {{checked}} links checked, {{flagged}} marked dangerous. cleanway.ai
mobile.report.privacy: This report is built on your phone from the links you checked here. It is not sent anywhere unless you share it.
mobile.score.subtitle: You checked links on {{days}} of the last 7 days
mobile.score.ring_a11y: You checked links on {{days}} of the last 7 days — {{band}}
mobile.score.honesty: This is not a measure of how safe you are. It only counts the days you checked a link in this app.
mobile.score.fact.dangerous_detail: {{num}} of the links you checked this week
mobile.score.empty_body: Check your first link, and this becomes a count of the days you check.
mobile.score.privacy: Worked out on your phone from your own check history. Nothing is sent anywhere.
mobile.settings.sign_in_desc: Keep your settings on all your devices
mobile.settings.signed_in_desc: Signed in. Your settings sync to this account.
mobile.settings.sign_out_confirm_body: Checks and history stay on this phone. Settings stop syncing until you sign in again.
mobile.settings.report_desc: A summary of the links you checked
mobile.settings.family_desc: Send alerts to people you care about, end-to-end encrypted
mobile.settings.skill_note: Used by the Cleanway browser extension to word its warnings. This app does not change its own wording yet. Saved on this phone, and to your account when you are signed in.
mobile.settings.skill_kids_desc: Short, strict warnings, with no button to open a dangerous site anyway.
mobile.settings.skill_regular_desc: The default. Clear warnings with a little detail.
mobile.settings.skill_granny_desc: Simple words, short sentences, no jargon.
mobile.settings.skill_pro_desc: Raw scores, threat types and technical detail.
mobile.settings.alerts_note: None of these work yet. Cleanway does not send notifications today, and it never watches your clipboard.
mobile.settings.push_desc: Tell me when a link looks dangerous
mobile.settings.auto_check_desc: Check a link as soon as I share it to Cleanway
mobile.settings.weekly_desc: Send me a summary once a week
mobile.settings.clear_confirm_body: This deletes every check saved on this phone. It cannot be undone.
mobile.settings.privacy_note: Your check history stays on this phone. When you check a link, only the website name goes to our servers.
mobile.settings.sync_failed_body: We couldn't reach your account, so this change won't show on your other devices yet. It will sync next time you change it while online.
mobile.settings.clear_done_body: All saved checks were removed from this phone.
mobile.settings.clear_failed_body: Something went wrong — your history is unchanged. Please try again.
mobile.family.title: Family Hub
mobile.family.signed_out_body: Sign in to set up Family Hub. When Cleanway blocks a scam in a family member's browser, you get an alert — end-to-end encrypted, so not even Cleanway can read it.
mobile.family.load_failed_body: We couldn't reach our servers, so we can't show your family right now. Your family is still there — please try again.
mobile.family.no_family_body: Get an alert when a scam is blocked in a loved one's browser. End-to-end encrypted — even Cleanway can't read the alerts.
mobile.family.join_invalid: That invite is not valid or has expired. Codes match upper and lower case exactly — pasting is the safest way.
mobile.family.members_load_failed: Couldn't load the member list right now. Pull down or come back later.
mobile.family.invite_desc: Makes a one-time code and PIN. Send them by text or read them out. Both appear once — keep them where the other person can read them.
mobile.family.alerts_empty: No alerts yet. When Cleanway blocks a scam in a family member's browser, it shows up here.
mobile.family.alerts_load_failed: Couldn't load alerts right now. This does not mean there are none — please try again.
mobile.family.alerts_undecryptable: {{n}} alert(s) couldn't be read on this phone. They were sent to a key this device doesn't have.
mobile.family.modal_title: Share this with your family member
mobile.family.modal_desc: Both appear once. After this closes you can't see them again — make another invite if you need to.
mobile.auth.sub_login: Sign in to keep your settings on all your devices
mobile.auth.sub_register: Free to start — no card needed for an account
mobile.auth.sub_reset: We'll email you a link to set a new password
mobile.auth.switch_to_register: Don't have an account? Sign up
mobile.auth.switch_to_login: Already have an account? Sign in
mobile.auth.privacy: With or without an account: we check website names on our servers — never your passwords, messages, or browsing history.
mobile.auth.confirm_body: We sent a confirmation link. Open it to activate your account.
mobile.auth.reset_sent_body: If an account exists for this address, we've sent a link to reset your password.
mobile.auth.generic_error: Something went wrong. Please try again.
mobile.auth.not_configured: Sign-in isn't available in this build. You can use everything else without an account.
mobile.onboarding.s1_title: Check anything before you tap it
mobile.onboarding.s1_desc: Paste a link, scan a QR code, or share anything suspicious straight to Cleanway. You get a plain answer and the reasons behind it.
mobile.onboarding.s2_desc: To check a link, only the website name is sent to our servers — never your passwords, messages, or browsing history.
mobile.onboarding.s3_desc: On Android, one setup step blocks known scam sites in every app. Brand-new scams can slip past any blocklist — that's what the check button is for.
